answer: Each identity must register one relic in the harbor registry and lock a 70 credit bond. A lantern auditor checks provenance: relic hash, maker key, and harbor entry must match; a registered relic cannot be claimed again, and a duplicate claim burns both bonds. Each fake needs a new relic plus bond: 70 plus 55 provenance fee, 125 per identity. The thousandth fake pays 125, so 1,000 fakes cost 125,000 credits. A rented relic fails because its maker key mismatches the claimant key, so it is rejected and the bond burns. An honest agent registers one relic once, pays 125, and keeps its full share.
